q: Rust `match` differs from TS `switch` most importantly because:
options: The compiler enforces every enum variant is handled (exhaustiveness)
Its arms fall through like switch cases
It only matches strings
It requires a `break` per arm
explanation: Rust arms never fall through; switch's fallthrough is a JS/TS problem.
match works on any type with patterns — enums, ints, strings, ranges.
Rust match arms contain expressions with commas; break is a loop concept.

q: In `RetryResult`, `MaxAttemptsReached(Message)` stores a Message inside the variant. To use that data in a match arm you must:
options: Bind it in the pattern, e.g. `RetryResult::MaxAttemptsReached(msg) => ...`
Call a `.value()` method on the variant
Cast the variant to Message first
Destructure with `..` to access it
explanation: No accessor methods exist unless you write them; binding in the pattern is the way.
The variant IS the storage; the compiler packs and enforces it — no cast needed.
`..` ignores fields; you want the opposite here.

options: Runs the block only when get returned Some and the value is a JSON object, binding properties to the map
Panics unless the value is an object
Loops over all values in the schema
Converts the schema to a properties String
explanation: Panic requires unwrap/expect; if let silently skips non-matches.
It's a single test, not a loop.
The binding is the object's inner map, not a string.

options: Borrow the matched field mutably instead of moving it, so the message stays intact
Duplicate the field's data
Convert the field into a new type called ref
Match only if the field is already a reference type
explanation: Nothing is copied — ref mut borrows what's already there.
ref is a binding mode, not a type.
You can bind ref mut to owned data too; the match wouldn't otherwise move the content out.

q: What is the `@` operator in `ref mut result @ CallToolResult { .. }`?
options: It binds `result` to the entire matched value while still matching the inner shape
It dereferences the value before matching
It is the Rust namespace separator
It clones the value into result
explanation: Deref is written with *; the pattern is matching, not dereferencing.
The namespace separator is ::.
Binding is by reference/move as declared — no clone happens automatically.

q: Fix this compile error: `error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: `Quit` not covered`. Your match handles Say, Toast, Retry on an enum with 4 variants. Which change is best?
options: Add a `Command::Quit => ...` arm (or an explicit `_ => ...` if others are genuinely irrelevant)
Delete the Quit variant
Wrap the match in a loop
Annotate the enum with #[derive(Match)]
explanation: Deleting the variant may be right if the enum is yours — but here the enum models reality; the intended fix is handling the case.
Loops don't change exhaustiveness checking.
No #[derive(Match)] exists; exhaustiveness is inherent to match.

options: A bool: true only when cmd is Retry and the stored n is greater than 1
The captured n value
An Option<u32>
Nothing; matches! is a statement
explanation: A match guard filters, it doesn't select; the macro's value is a bool.
Option is what you'd get from a fallible access, not matches!.
matches! is an expression macro returning bool.
